headline: Singapore's government technology agency and Google DeepMind are building an AI model that warns Android phone users of scams as they happen, without sending their messages to a server.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a government and Google project with a clear consumer benefit, but no launch date or test results are given.
importance_line: Phone users in Singapore may get an early warning before they send money or give up passwords while keeping messages private, but no launch date has been given, it targets Android first and no test results are shown.
summary: CNA reports that Josephine Teo, Singapore's minister for digital development and information, said on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 that the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) is working with Google DeepMind, Google's AI research lab, on an on-device AI model for Android phones that reads conversation patterns locally, without sending data to outside servers, and shows a warning when it detects a scam. Google says the model is tuned on local scam stories, such as people posing as banks and public bodies, and that details on how users can install it will be announced soon.
notes: CNA full text read; the quantum-safe migration part of the same speech is not used.
